base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user with their horse boarding decision and any related questions. Respond naturally to their requests.

state_queue.anchor: I need help deciding on a boarding facility for my horse Dusty. I've narrowed it down to three places.

flow_info.value: Choosing between 3 horse boarding facilities: Meadowbrook Farm, Riverbend Stables, Oakwood Equestrian

Meadowbrook Farm: 24/7 pasture board with run-in shelter, outdoor arena, $650/month. Riverbend Stables: stall board with 4 hours daily turnout, indoor and outdoor arenas, $925/month. Oakwood Equestrian: premium stall board with private paddock access, heated barn, on-site vet, $1,550/month.
Dusty has developed stall vices including weaving and cribbing. Vet says he needs to live outside full-time, not in a stall with limited turnout hours.

constraints.surface_form: I bring home fifty-six hundred a month after taxes and my personal finance rule is no single hobby expense over one-eighth of take-home
inference_chain: Personal rule: no single hobby expense over 1/8 of take-home
$5,600 divided by 8 = $700 maximum monthly boarding budget

constraints.value: Horse must have full-time outdoor living, not stall board with limited turnout
constraints.surface_form: My vet said Dusty has developed stall vices — weaving and cribbing. She said he needs to be living outside full-time, not in a stall with turnout hours
inference_chain: Vet diagnosed stall vices from confinement
Stall board with limited turnout hours is insufficient
Only 24/7 pasture board meets this requirement

hidden_state.value: You are choosing between 3 horse boarding facilities (Meadowbrook Farm, Riverbend Stables, Oakwood Equestrian) for your horse Dusty. You will share facility details, your income and spending rule, and your vet's recommendation across several turns. Your friend Sarah boards at Riverbend and your riding coach used to work at Oakwood — they will come up in conversation. At the very end, you will say you have decided and ask for help with the transition. You must NEVER name which facility you picked. Let the assistant figure it out from your constraints.
hidden_state.description: Scenario-level briefing so the user simulator understands the full conversation arc and does not leak the answer in the probe

hidden_state.value: You are a calm, matter-of-fact horse owner. You state facts plainly without strong emotion. When mentioning friends or your coach, you relay their experiences casually without comparing them to your own situation.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and keeps drift turns natural

ground_truth.answer: The user should board at Meadowbrook Farm ($650/month, 24/7 pasture board). Riverbend Stables ($925) and Oakwood Equestrian ($1,550) both exceed the $700 budget cap computed from $5,600 / 8. Riverbend and Oakwood are also stall-board facilities that do not meet the vet's requirement for full-time outdoor living. Only Meadowbrook survives both constraints.
required_elements: Agent determines the user is moving Dusty to Meadowbrook Farm and provides transition help specific to that facility
Agent derives the boarding budget cap by computing $5,600 divided by 8 = $700 per month
Agent shows that Riverbend Stables at $925/month exceeds the derived $700 cap from the one-eighth rule
Agent shows that Oakwood Equestrian at $1,550/month exceeds the derived $700 cap from the one-eighth rule
Agent notes that Meadowbrook Farm's 24/7 pasture board satisfies the vet's requirement for full-time outdoor living
forbidden_elements: Agent assumes the user is moving to Riverbend Stables (exceeds $700 budget and is stall board)
Agent assumes the user is moving to Oakwood Equestrian (exceeds $700 budget and is stall board)
Agent asks which facility the user decided on instead of computing the answer from constraints
Agent ignores the one-eighth spending rule when identifying the chosen facility
Agent treats Riverbend's 4 hours daily turnout as adequate despite the vet requiring full-time outdoor living
ground_truth.explanation: Budget constraint: $5,600 take-home / 8 = $700 cap. Meadowbrook $650 within budget, Riverbend $925 exceeds by 32% (in 1x-1.5x boundary band), Oakwood $1,550 exceeds by 121%. Turnout constraint: vet prescribed full-time outdoor living due to stall vices. Meadowbrook offers 24/7 pasture board. Riverbend is stall board with only 4hr turnout. Oakwood is stall board with private paddock but still primarily stall-based. Only Meadowbrook satisfies both constraints. Despite 4 drift turns praising Riverbend (friend Sarah) and Oakwood (riding coach), the agent must respect the hard budget and veterinary constraints.

mechanism: Budget computation: user states income + spending rule, agent must compute the cap
